title: ops-surgical-kit: idempotent admin wrappers for transactional repair flows
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current runbooks-as-tasks surface exposes raw step execution to oncall engineers. Many remediation steps are not safe to run more than once, lack transparent cost/latency estimates, and provide poor fidelity in telemetry for post-mortems.

Goal: Build a lightweight "ops-surgical-kit" library and runtime shim that makes admin utilities transactional and idempotent by default, provides a dry-run / preview mode, emits structured per-step telemetry, and supports automatic checkpoints and rollback hints. This will be used by runbooks-as-tasks, the admin CLI, and the operator console.

Scope:
- A minimal runtime shim (python + typescript clients) that wraps existing admin commands with: idempotency tokens, optimistic checkpointing, and a standardized result schema.
- An RPC adapter for the runbook executor that can replay failed steps safely and mark steps as "safe-retry" vs "one-shot".
- Dry-run mode that executes validation checks and cost/latency estimates without side effects.
- Telemetry schema and tracing integration (trace id + step id + outcome + cost_estimate) wired into Console tracing and the incident timeline.
- A small set of example repairlets (key-rotate, queue-drain, redis-compaction) rewritten to the wrapper API as reference implementations.

Non-Goals: Rewriting all admin tooling to a new language or vastly changing permission model. This is an interoperability shim to be adopted incrementally.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Wrapper library published (pip/npm) and used by at least 3 reference repairlets.
2) Runbook executor can mark and replay steps conservatively in staging with no data-loss incidents during a 2-week soak.
3) Dry-run produces full validation and cost/latency estimates visible in the Console preview panel.
4) Per-step telemetry appears in tracing and supports drilldown to the PR and runbook invocation.

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: Race conditions on concurrent repairlets that touch the same resource. Mitigation: optimistic locking and a conflict-detection header + automatic abort with safe retry hints.
- Risk: Misclassification of one-shot steps; emergency escape hatch will allow operator to elevate and run with explicit confirmation.

Docs & related artifacts: Confluence design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OP/pages/ops-surgical-kit-design, Drive prototype spec: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1OpsSurgicalKitSpec, proposal PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-surgeon/pull/321
